adding_an_analysis.Rmd
library(basictabler)
library(dplyr)
library(htmltools)
library(beFAIR)

🚧 Under construction 🚧

The Analysis Pillar

The analysis pillar is one of three data pillars in beFAIR. It stores data that represents some form of interpretation applied to study and/or experimental data — ranging from standard pre-processing pipelines to elaborate cluster analyses. Examples include fitting an ELISA dose-response curve, running a Self-Organizing Map (SOM) clustering pipeline on CyTOF measurements, or applying a custom statistical model.

Because analyses may draw on samples from multiple studies and on the outputs of multiple experiments, they are linked to the rest of the database via experiment_id and study_id references stored in their meta.yaml.

All analyses live inside the FAIRground directory. beFAIR directly sources each ETL script, which must produce a databook object and load it into the database. Analyses can declare explicit dependencies on upstream database tables (e.g. cytofpanel from a specific experiment) via the dependencies field in meta.yaml; these are tracked in table_dependency and used to flag when upstream data has changed.

#> [1] "analyses"       "beFAIR.Rproj"   "codebooks"      "common"        
#> [5] "experiments"    "fairground.yml" "logs"           "studies"
overviewFAIRground()
#> Warning in overviewFAIRground(): 'overviewFAIRground' is deprecated.
#> Use 'FAIRgroundOverview' instead.
#> See help("Deprecated")
#> 
#>  FAIRground Overview Summary
#> 
#> STUDIES: 0 rows × 0 columns
#>  (no data available)
#> 
#> EXPERIMENTS: 0 rows × 0 columns
#>  (no data available)
#> 
#> ANALYSES: 0 rows × 0 columns
#>  (no data available)

Internal delivery

An analysis is added with addAnalysis(). You must supply a unique name and a scientific type. We recommend following the naming convention [study]_[type]_[descriptor].

The supported analysis types are: "SOM", "OMIQ", "ELISA", "Array", "Luminex", and "Glycoprofiling".

addAnalysis("CoHSI1_SOM_surface", "SOM")
#> Analysis added: CoHSI1_SOM_surface. Add the additional analysis information to the meta.yaml file located at: analyses/CoHSI1_SOM_surface/meta.yaml
#>

The analysis folder

A new folder is created under analyses/ named after the analysis:

list.files("analyses/CoHSI1_SOM_surface")
#> [1] "data"      "meta.yaml" "scripts"

It contains three components:

  • meta.yaml: metadata about the analysis, pre-filled from the base analysis codebook and the type-specific codebook (here analysis_som).
  • data/: for storing data location descriptors (YAML files), same pattern as studies and experiments.
  • scripts/: ETL R scripts drafted automatically for the chosen type.

meta.yaml

The meta.yaml stores essential metadata about the analysis. beFAIR pre-fills fields from the analysis codebook and any type-specific extension (e.g. analysis_som adds pipeline_location and pipeline_description). Fill in the missing values before running databaseUpdate().

#> analysis_id: Ac6be45
#> name: CoHSI1_SOM_surface
#> type: SOM
#> study_ids: .na
#> experiment_ids: .na
#> analysis_ids: .na
#> table_dependecies: .na
#> publication_pmid: .na
#> description: .na
#> project_location: .na
#> source_ready: .na
#> git_repo: .na
#> owner: .na
#> version: '1.0'
#> SOM_settings: .na

Key fields to complete:

Field Description
study_ids Semicolon-separated IDs of studies whose samples were used
experiment_ids Semicolon-separated IDs of source experiments
description Free-text description of the analysis
pipeline_location (SOM only) Path or URL to the SOM pipeline

The dependencies field is initially empty. Fill it in to declare which upstream database tables this analysis uses (e.g. - cytofpanel[Eef536a]). beFAIR will track these in table_dependency and flag the analysis as out-of-date when upstream data changes.

ETL scripts

For a SOM analysis, two ETL scripts are drafted:

list.files("analyses/CoHSI1_SOM_surface/scripts")
#> [1] "som_clusterphenotype.R" "som_measurement.R"
  • som_clusterphenotype.R: loads the cluster phenotype table (one row per SOM cluster, with marker expression profiles).
  • som_measurement.R: loads per-sample SOM measurements (cluster frequencies or similar metrics).

Each script follows the standard beFAIR ETL pattern — it must produce a databook object and end with rm(list = setdiff(ls(), c("databook"))). See ?draftScript for details.
